title: Immediate Reclamation of Shared Resources
pattern: Immediately freeing or deallocating a shared resource after removing its pointer from a global data structure, without waiting for concurrent reader threads to exit.
why_bad: Reader threads that were actively traversing the structure before its removal will still hold raw pointers to the item, causing a crash or use-after-free when they access it.
detection: A concurrent data structure update deletes a node and immediately deallocates it without invoking synchronize_rcu(), hazard pointers, or a reference counter.
counterexample: Using RCU or hazard pointers to defer reclamation until all pre-existing reader threads have completed.
fix: Introduce a grace-period deferral before deallocating the memory: `list_remove(item); synchronize_rcu(); free(item);`.
